svg.text: The wraparound problem (and the mask that fixes it)
The 64 bits are really ONE long line. Rows exist only in our heads.
Bits 24–39 of the uint64_t, written in order:
h4 (bit 31) and a5 (bit 32) are neighbours in the integer, even though they sit on opposite edges of the board.
Why it works: after an east shift, the ONLY way a bit can land on the a-file is by wrapping from the h-file, so we erase the a-file.
The same idea in reverse: after a west shift (>> 1), erase the h-file with NOT_H_FILE = 0x7F7F7F7F7F7F7F7FULL.
North/south shifts (<< 8, >> 8) need no mask: bits pushed past bit 63 or below bit 0 fall off the integer = off the board.
Diagonals mix both: north-east (<< 9) and south-east (>> 7) need NOT_A_FILE; north-west (<< 7) and south-west (>> 9) need NOT_H_FILE.
